title: Sonam Wangchuk Removed From Jantar Mantar Protest Site and Taken to Hospital on Day 21 of Hunger Strike
excerpt: Delhi Police moved the climate activist to Safdarjung Hospital following a Delhi High Court order, as supporters report chaos and alleged police force at the protest site.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Sonam Wangchuk was removed from protest site on Day 21 of his hunger strike due to health concerns.
  • He has lost over 9 kg since starting his fast on June 28, demanding minister's resignation.
  • Chaos erupted at the protest site, with reports of police violence against supporters.
  • A planned march to Parliament on July 20 by the Cockroach Janta Party is still on schedule.
  • Wangchuk's hunger strike has garnered significant political and celebrity support across India.

  • The activist was shifted to Safdarjung Hospital. Supporters reported chaos at the site, with CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke allegedly beaten and detained.
  • Wangchuk has lost over 9 kg since beginning his fast on June 28, demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over NEET irregularities.
  • A planned march to Parliament on July 20 by the Cockroach Janta Party remains on schedule despite the removal.

Police Move on Day 21

Authorities in Delhi removed climate activist Sonam Wangchuk from the Jantar Mantar protest site on Friday and shifted him to Safdarjung Hospital, on the 21st day of a hunger strike that has become one of the most visible acts of defiance against the Modi government in recent memory.

Delhi Police said the action was taken in compliance with a Delhi High Court order issued earlier in the week, which directed authorities to ensure daily medical check-ups and intervene if Wangchuk's condition deteriorated. Doctors had warned that his prolonged fast had reached a critical stage, with the risk of organ damage increasing.

The removal sparked chaos at the protest site. The Cockroach Janta Party, the youth-led political movement at the center of the demonstration, said its founder Abhijeet Dipke was beaten and detained by police during the operation. The party's account has not been independently verified, and police have not commented on the specific allegation.

""I am weak from the outside but very strong inside," he said, according to reports from the Hindu BusinessLine."

Twenty Days Without Food

Wangchuk, 59, began his indefinite hunger strike on June 28 in solidarity with CJP's sit-in protest demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-UG examination paper leak scandal that affected millions of students in May. The educator and engineer — widely known as the inspiration behind Aamir Khan's character in the 2009 film 3 Idiots — has lost more than 9 kg since the fast began.

On Thursday, just hours before his removal, Wangchuk addressed supporters from the protest stage. "I am weak from the outside but very strong inside," he said, according to reports from the Hindu BusinessLine. "I will stay alive till July 20 at any cost. If you don't come and July 20 is not successful, I will come back as a ghost."

Political Support and Opposition Pressure

The hunger strike has drawn support from across India's political opposition and entertainment industry. AAP leader and former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal visited the protest site and urged the Centre to heed the students' demands, suggesting Prime Minister Modi should appoint Wangchuk as the next education minister. Congress leaders including Shashi Tharoor and K.C. Venugopal have appealed to Wangchuk to end his fast while pledging to continue pressing the government through parliamentary channels.

Bollywood actors Shabana Azmi, Soni Razdan, Aamir Khan, and Anurag Kashyap have also expressed concern over Wangchuk's condition. At the London Indian Film Festival, Aamir Khan clarified that the film 3 Idiots "was not based on Sonam Wangchuk" but said he was deeply concerned about the activist's health.

What Comes Next

The CJP, founded by 30-year-old Dipke, has gained 22 million Instagram followers since its launch in May, according to Reuters. The party has called for a march to Parliament on July 20 to press its demands, and Wangchuk had been rallying supporters for the event even as his condition worsened. Whether the hospitalization will galvanize or disperse the movement remains to be seen.

The Education Ministry and government spokesperson have not publicly responded to the protesters' demands. The NEET controversy continues to be one of the most politically sensitive issues facing the Modi government's third term.
